about.body:
The figures come from the finance ministry's Budget Information System (rozpocet.sk), where Bratislava reports its budget and spending every quarter. The site does not change them, it only presents them clearly. If a figure is not published, the site says so and never estimates.

What differs from the state budget. A city has no chapters or ministries, so spending is shown by purpose (the official functional classification) and by city organisation. The data is quarterly, not monthly. Spending and revenue include financial operations: loan repayments, loans taken and money from previous years.

Difference from the city's own documents. The approved budget in this system does not match the amount in the budget the city publishes on its website. For 2026, for example, the city council approved a budget of €760.5 million on 6 November 2025, while in the budget system the city reports an approved budget of €835.4 million. The site uses the system's data because only that is published in machine-readable form together with spending. The city's original documents are linked in the sources below.

The city budget does not include the budgets of the 17 city boroughs or the finances of city-owned companies.
about.licence: Terms of use of the data:

glossary: The plan of the capital's revenue and spending for one year. It is approved by the city council.
The official way of sorting spending by what it is for: transport, education, waste and so on. All municipalities use it.
The budget the city reports in the budget system as approved. It can differ from the amount in the council's resolution.
The budget after changes during the year.
Money the city has actually paid out. During the year it is the total since 1 January.
A city organisation whose revenue and spending are entirely part of the city budget, such as a home for seniors or an elementary art school.
A city organisation that also has its own income and receives a contribution from the city, such as the zoo, the museum or the city forests.
Loans taken and repaid, and money moved from funds and previous years. They are not regular revenue or spending.
